q1_issues.issue: (Inheritance current_warden current) exposes a modifier genus that is not licensed: "current" is a relational/rank adjective failing the predication test (*"the warden is current"), which the instruction set says is never exposed as a modifier genus, and it falls outside the three licensed categories (gradable, positional/cardinal, material adjective).

q2_gaps: A capitalized multi-word OFFICE TITLE embedding a proper noun, used as a predicate nominal ("is the current Cauldron Hall Warden"): the mechanical casing rule ("the name is exactly its capitalized run of words") makes "Cauldron Hall Warden" one name symbol, while the proper-noun-premodifier rule splits it into the name "Cauldron Hall" plus a separately-parsed common-noun head; the instruction set states no precedence, and applying the casing rule literally would put a name symbol in a class position.
notes: The chosen split (name cauldron_hall with its in-name kind atom, head phrase parsed normally, opaque Possession linking Hesper to the named entity) follows the Northgate-spokesman pattern faithfully; note that it truncates the capitalized run in the Name string.
